facts.content: Patient reports pain with urination for 6 days.
facts.source_text: CC: "Hurts when I pee" (dysuria) x6 days

facts.content: Patient has burning and stinging with urination.
Patient reports malodorous urine.
Patient has intermittent midline suprapubic or lower abdominal pain rated 7 out of 10.
Patient reports spotting or visible blood in the urine for 6 days.
facts.source_text: Spotting/visible blood in urine for 6 days

facts.content: Patient reports no fever.
Patient reports no loin or back pain.
Patient reports no vaginal discharge.
Patient reports no recent sexual intercourse.
Patient has a history of irritable bowel syndrome.
Past medical history includes IBS.
Patient reports taking Mebavin 200 mg three times daily.
Patient is allergic to clindamycin.
Patient lives with friends.
Patient works as a support worker.
Patient drinks alcohol occasionally at about one glass of wine per week.
Patient is a non-smoker.
Clinician suspects an acute lower urinary tract infection or acute cystitis.
facts.source_text: Suspected acute lower urinary tract infection (acute cystitis)

facts.content: The suspected acute cystitis is supported by 6 days of dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, and hematuria with the patient afebrile and without flank pain.
facts.source_text: 6 days dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, hematuria; afebrile, no flank pain.

facts.content: Hematuria is assessed as being associated with the current urinary symptoms.
facts.source_text: Hematuria associated with current urinary symptoms.

facts.content: A 3-day course of oral antibiotics was prescribed.
facts.source_text: Rx: 3-day course of oral antibiotics prescribed

facts.content: The antibiotic prescription was sent to the patient-requested pharmacy at Knightsbridge practice for the patient to collect and start promptly.
facts.source_text: sent to patient-requested pharmacy (Knightsbridge practice) — patient to collect and start promptly.

facts.content: Patient was advised to increase oral fluids to approximately 2.5 to 3 liters per day.
Patient was advised to consider drinking cranberry juice.
Patient was advised to consider over-the-counter sachets from the pharmacy to alter urine acidity as discussed.
facts.source_text: OTC sachets from pharmacy to alter urine acidity as discussed.

facts.content: Patient was advised to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature.
Patient was instructed to return or seek care if pain worsens, a new fever develops, loin or flank pain occurs, inability to pass urine develops, or if episodes recur.
facts.source_text: return/seek care if worsening pain, new fever, loin/flank pain, inability to pass urine, or recurrent episodes.

facts.content: Follow-up is advised only if symptoms do not resolve after treatment or if they recur.
facts.source_text: Follow-up only if symptoms do not resolve after treatment or recur.
